In another match, the low serum chloride level was found to be associated with an increased risk of total, CVD, and non-CVD mortalities in a population-based study. However, it did not indicate any association between low serum chloride levels and asthma symptom persistence among adolescents.

The question about whether higher body mass index contributes to worse asthma control in an urban population with asthma was not directly addressed by the retrieved matches, but one study found that weight loss may not be an appropriate strategy to improve asthma control in this specific population.
